title: Rigidification and coherent enriched-diagram comparison
statement:
Fix universes $\mathcal U\in\mathcal U'$; small means $\mathcal U$-small and all categories under discussion fit in $\mathcal U'$. Use the infinity-category conventions of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and simplicial model categories and the nerve $N_{\mathrm{hc}}$ as defined in [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization]. For a small simplicial set $K$, let $\mathfrak C[K]$ be the simplicial category obtained by taking the colimit, over the ordinary category of simplices $\Delta^n\to K$, of the simplicial thickenings of $[n]$ defined there. It is left adjoint to $N_{\mathrm{hc}}$. A Dwyer--Kan equivalence of simplicial categories means a simplicial functor inducing weak homotopy equivalences on every mapping simplicial set and an essentially surjective functor on the categories with morphisms $\pi_0$ of those sets.

For every small simplicial category $T$ whose mapping simplicial sets are Kan, the counit $\mathfrak C[N_{\mathrm{hc}}T]\to T$ is a Dwyer--Kan equivalence. Let $u:\mathfrak C[K]\to\mathcal C$ be a Dwyer--Kan equivalence between small simplicial categories (with no local Kan hypothesis on $\mathcal C$), and let $\mathcal M$ be a combinatorial simplicial model category; combinatorial means locally presentable with both model weak factorization systems generated by small sets, and locally presentable means generated under $\kappa$-filtered colimits, for some regular $\kappa$, by a small set of objects whose Hom functors preserve such colimits. Assume the category $\operatorname{Fun}_{\Delta}(\mathcal C,\mathcal M)$ of simplicial functors is equipped with its simplicial projective model structure (weak equivalences and fibrations are objectwise). There is a categorical equivalence, in the sense of [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure],
$$N_{\mathrm{hc}}\bigl(\operatorname{Fun}_{\Delta}(\mathcal C,\mathcal M)^{cf}\bigr)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Fun}\bigl(K,N_{\mathrm{hc}}(\mathcal M^{cf})\bigr).$$
It is the comparison induced by enriched evaluation and $u$, so it identifies evaluation at each vertex and the arrows and coherent compositions of diagrams. Universes may be enlarged so that the entire category $\mathcal M$ is available; equivalently one may use the full category as a chunk in the statement of the comparison theorem.

source.place: Theorem 2.2.5.1 (printed p. 89), counit discussed in proof of Corollary 2.2.5.6 (printed p. 93); Example A.3.4.4 and Definition A.3.4.9 (printed pp. 885, 888), which make the full model category a chunk of itself and its projective diagram category; Proposition 4.2.4.4 and Remark 4.2.4.5 (printed p. 258), allowing the full chunk after universe enlargement. Read online, not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this theorem.

proof.text: The stated colimit construction is adjoint to the nerve. A simplicial functor from $\mathfrak C[K]$ to $T$ is a family of simplicial functors $\mathfrak C[\Delta^n]\to T$, one for every simplex of $K$, compatible with all simplex operators. By the defining formula for $N_{\mathrm{hc}}T$, this is exactly a simplicial map $K\to N_{\mathrm{hc}}T$: on a simplex use its member of that family. The inverse assigns to a simplicial map its composites with all simplices of $K$. These two assignments undo one another and commute with maps in both variables.

source.place: Section 1.1.5, defining adjunction by extension from the simplex thickenings.

proof.text: For a locally Kan simplicial category $T$, it is fibrant in the Bergner model structure. The adjunction in [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison] is a Quillen equivalence and all Joyal simplicial sets are cofibrant. Its cofibrant-to-fibrant test applied to $\mathfrak C[N_{\mathrm{hc}}T]\to T$ identifies this counit with the identity of the fibrant object $N_{\mathrm{hc}}T$ under adjunction. The identity is a categorical equivalence, so the counit is a Bergner weak equivalence, namely a Dwyer--Kan equivalence. This verifies both mapping-space equivalences and essential surjectivity, rather than only the latter.

source.place: Theorem 2.2.5.1 and the proof of Corollary 2.2.5.6, printed pp.89,93.

proof.text:
Put $I=\mathfrak C[K]$. It is Bergner cofibrant because $\mathfrak C$ is left Quillen and $K$ is Joyal cofibrant [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison]. The projective structures of [lem-coef-simplicial-projective-model-calculus] make $\mathcal A=\mathcal M$ and $\mathcal A^I$ combinatorial simplicial model categories. Their bifibrant diagrams are objectwise bifibrant, so enriched evaluation defines $e:(\mathcal A^I)^{cf}\times I\to\mathcal A^{cf}$. For small $D$, currying a simplicial functor $D\to\mathcal A^I$ gives a simplicial functor $I\times D\to\mathcal A$: the values are $F(d)(i)$ and naturality in the two variables is the same commuting equation. This is an isomorphism of ordinary categories $(\mathcal A^I)^D\cong\mathcal A^{I\times D}$ preserving and reflecting weak equivalences, since on both sides those are weak equivalences at every pair $(i,d)$. Apply [lem-coef-simplicial-diagram-equivalence-classes] first with target $\mathcal A^I$ and index $D$, and then with target $\mathcal A$ and index $I\times D$. It gives natural bijections
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{h\mathrm{sCat}}(D,(\mathcal A^I)^{cf})\cong\pi_0((\mathcal A^I)^D)\cong\pi_0(\mathcal A^{I\times D})\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{h\mathrm{sCat}}(I\times D,\mathcal A^{cf}).$$
Following a bifibrant representative through these maps shows that this bijection is induced by $e$. No cofibrancy of $I\times D$ is asserted or needed: the unrestricted class-bijection holds for every small simplicial category.

source.place: Proposition A.3.4.13 and its proof by two applications of Proposition A.3.4.12, printed p.890.

proof.text:
Let $U$ be a small $I$-chunk of $\mathcal A$, in the sense of [lem-coef-simplicial-small-chunks]. The inclusions $(U^I)^{cf}\subseteq(\mathcal A^I)^{cf}$ and $U^{cf}\subseteq\mathcal A^{cf}$ induce injections on derived Hom sets by [lem-coef-simplicial-fully-faithful-homotopy-image], with images determined by essential image on objects. Under Step 3, the first image condition means that for each object $d$ of $D$, the corresponding $I$-diagram is weakly equivalent to one represented in $(U^I)^{cf}$. The second image condition means that all its values at $(i,d)$ are isomorphic to objects of $U^{cf}$ in the ordinary homotopy category of $\mathcal A$. These conditions are equivalent: one implication follows by evaluation. For the reverse implication apply the essential-image test with source $I$ to factor the derived map $I\to\mathcal A^{cf}$ through $U^{cf}$. The restricted class-bijection of [lem-coef-simplicial-diagram-equivalence-classes], applicable because $I$ is cofibrant and $U$ is an $I$-chunk, supplies an $I$-diagram with values in $U$ representing this derived map. Replace that diagram projectively cofibrant fibrant inside $U^I$, using the chunk closure. Compatibility of the restricted bijection with the unrestricted one says that its unrestricted class is the original one. Thus Step 3 restricts to natural bijections
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{h\mathrm{sCat}}(D,(U^I)^{cf})\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{h\mathrm{sCat}}(I\times D,U^{cf}),$$
still induced by evaluation. The empty-family closure in the chunk definition is what supplies the replacements remaining in $U$ and $U^I$.

source.place: Corollary A.3.4.14, using the essential-image criterion of Corollary A.3.4.11 and the restricted form of Proposition A.3.4.12, printed pp.889-890.

proof.text:
For small $U$ as above, all categories in Step 4 are small. Transfer its natural bijections through the derived equivalence between the Joyal and Bergner homotopy categories [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison]. Products are preserved: the rigidification comparison for products and the Joyal exponential formula are supplied by [lem-coef-joyal-homotopy-exponentials]. With a simplicial test object $L$ and $D=\mathfrak C[L]$, Step 4 becomes
$$[L,N_{\mathrm{hc}}((U^I)^{cf})]_{\mathrm J}\cong[L\times K,N_{\mathrm{hc}}(U^{cf})]_{\mathrm J}\cong[L,\operatorname{Fun}(K,N_{\mathrm{hc}}(U^{cf}))]_{\mathrm J}.$$
The map inducing it is the adjoint of the coherent nerve of evaluation, precomposed with the adjunction unit $K\to N_{\mathrm{hc}}I$. Consequently the actual evaluation comparison induces a bijection on Hom sets from every $L$. To see it is an isomorphism in the Joyal homotopy category, use the target as $L$ to obtain a right inverse, and then use injectivity with the source as $L$ to show it is also a left inverse. Apply [lem-coef-model-localization-detects-weak-equivalences] to the Joyal model category: an actual map is an isomorphism in its model homotopy category exactly when it is a weak equivalence. Thus this comparison is a categorical equivalence.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 4.2.4.4, homotopy-category exponential argument, printed p.258; Corollary A.3.4.14 and Proposition 1.2.7.3.

proof.text:
Remove the small-chunk restriction without treating a large category as a small one. Fix a regular $\kappa$ larger than the number of simplices and objects in $I$ and $K$. By [lem-coef-simplicial-small-chunks], every small full subcategory of $\mathcal A$ lies in a small $I$-chunk. The poset of such chunks, ordered by inclusion, is $\kappa$-filtered: for fewer than $\kappa$ given chunks, take their union of objects and then a containing small $I$-chunk. It covers $\mathcal A$. Each simplex of $N_{\mathrm{hc}}((\mathcal A^I)^{cf})$ uses only finitely many $I$-diagrams and their small set of values; choose a chunk containing these values. Because each chunk is full, the entire simplex then lies in $N_{\mathrm{hc}}((U^I)^{cf})$. On the target, an $n$-simplex is a map $K\times\Delta^n\to N_{\mathrm{hc}}(\mathcal A^{cf})$, and its small collection of image objects also lies in a chunk. Thus both the source and target of the evaluation comparison are the degreewise filtered colimits of their chunk versions. Fullness also shows that equality of two represented simplices is equality in a common chunk, so these are colimits, not just surjections onto the sets of simplices. If necessary enlarge the bookkeeping universe to make this poset small; the diagram/model constructions remain those for the original small $I$ and $K$. The chunk comparisons commute with inclusions, since they all come from the same evaluation. Step 5 and [lem-coef-joyal-filtered-equivalences] therefore prove
$$N_{\mathrm{hc}}((\mathcal A^{\mathfrak C[K]})^{cf})\simeq\operatorname{Fun}(K,N_{\mathrm{hc}}(\mathcal A^{cf})).$$

source.place: Proof of Proposition 4.2.4.4, first paragraph (small-chunk reduction), and Lemma A.3.4.15, printed pp.258,890-891.

proof.text: Return to $u:I=\mathfrak C[K]\to\mathcal C$. By [lem-coef-simplicial-projective-model-calculus], $u_!\dashv u^*$ is a simplicial Quillen equivalence of combinatorial projective diagram models, without a local Kan assumption on $\mathcal C$. The full diagram category $\mathcal A^I$ is a chunk of itself by [lem-coef-simplicial-small-chunks]. Its empty-cofan factorization gives an enriched cofibrant replacement $q:Q\Rightarrow\operatorname{id}$ through trivial fibrations. Restriction of a bifibrant $F$ is objectwise bifibrant and projectively fibrant; hence $Q(u^*F)$ is projectively bifibrant. Apply [lem-coef-derived-restriction-bifibrant-nerve-equivalence] with $L=u_!$, $R=u^*$. It identifies $N_{\mathrm{hc}}(Qu^*)$ with derived restriction and proves it is an equivalence between the two bifibrant diagram nerves. This proves the derived-restriction assertion of the returned step 7 without assuming that $u^*$ preserves projective cofibrancy.

source.place: Propositions A.3.3.7-A.3.3.8 and Remark 4.2.4.5; localization-to-bifibrant-nerve comparison as in HA Theorem 1.3.4.20.

proof.text: Write $c_I,c_{\mathcal C}$ for the specified evaluation comparisons. Use [lem-coef-enriched-evaluation-replacement-coherence] with $B=(\mathcal A^{\mathcal C})^{cf}$, $H_0=Qu^*$, $H_1=u^*$, the replacement $q$, and $a:K\to N_{\mathrm{hc}}I$ the adjunction unit from Step 1. The projective model and evaluation clauses of [lem-coef-simplicial-projective-model-calculus] ensure that $B$ is locally Kan and both families take objectwise bifibrant values. Each $q_F(i)$ is an objectwise weak equivalence, so the lemma gives a natural equivalence $c_I\circ N_{\mathrm{hc}}(Qu^*)\simeq c_{\mathcal C}$; its components are precisely the evaluated replacement maps. Step 6 proves $c_I$ is a categorical equivalence, and Step 7 proves the same for $N_{\mathrm{hc}}(Qu^*)$. Their composite is therefore an equivalence, as is the naturally equivalent map $c_{\mathcal C}$. This proves the comparison for the specified $u$, including non-locally-Kan $\mathcal C$, with the same evaluation map.

source.place: Propositions A.3.3.7-A.3.3.8 and Remark 4.2.4.5; localization-to-bifibrant-nerve comparison as in HA Theorem 1.3.4.20.

proof.text: At a vertex $k$ of $K$, the evaluation adjunction used above sends a diagram $F$ to $F(u(k))$. On an $n$-simplex it applies the same enriched evaluation functor to the simplex thickening together with the map of thickenings specified by $u$; therefore its faces, degeneracies and compositions are the images of those of the diagram, with no independent choice at arrows or higher simplices. This proves the asserted compatibility with vertices, arrows and coherent compositions. The size argument in Step 6 also proves the full-category/chunk formulation: the whole model category is a chunk and its comparison is obtained from its small chunks.

lean.note: Uses the landed simplex-colimit rigidification, DK predicate, and HomotopicalAlgebra.CombinatorialModelCategory from the landed model-colimit localization interface. Helpers specify the actual enriched end and its projective model structure; no assumed equivalence or arbitrary comparison is supplied as input. The output comparison is characterized on every coherent simplex and mapping simplex. The small index universe u and model object universe w are independent.
